description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/lib.rs:19-27 (module-level doc on memory feature):

> Enable the `memory` feature to expose the `memory::MemoryBackend`
> reference implementation of [`SharingBackend`]. ... **Not production.**
> API stability is opt-in via this feature and may break across minor
> versions while the crate is pre-1.0.

This stability disclaimer applies ONLY to the `memory` module.
Everything else in the public surface — `SharingBackend` trait,
`register_sharing_handlers`, the 10 `handle_*` functions, the URI
re-exports, the 13 re-exports from `jmap-server` — has no stability
statement at all.

A caller reading this crate's documentation has no answer to:

1. Does the workspace's pre-1.0 \"minor version may break\" policy
   apply to `SharingBackend`? The trait has 4 methods; adding a 5th
   would break every external impl. Is that allowed in 0.x?

2. Does it apply to the `handle_*` functions? Are these functions
   stable API for callers that bypass `register_sharing_handlers`?
   Looking at the tests in `principal.rs:309-403`, the handler
   functions ARE intended for direct caller use (the tests invoke
   `handle_principal_get` etc. directly).

3. Does it apply to the re-export blocks in `backend.rs:13-17`?
   These re-export 13 types from `jmap-server` plus 2 from
   `jmap-sharing-types`. A semver bump on either upstream cascades
   here.

The canonical mail-server has the same gap (its module-level doc at
`lib.rs:31-40` carries the same `memory`-only stability statement).
Filing here scoped to sharing-server; the workspace-wide propagation
is a separate follow-up.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a downstream
consumer pinning `jmap-sharing-server = \"^0.1\"` cannot reason
about whether a minor version bump (0.1.1 → 0.2.0) is allowed to
break their `SharingBackend` impl. If the workspace's intent is
\"all 0.x APIs are unstable\" then say that. If the intent is
\"the trait and handler signatures are stable; only `memory` is
opt-in unstable\", then say that.

Resolution: extend the crate-level rustdoc with one paragraph
stating the workspace stability policy for pre-1.0. Cross-reference
to a workspace AGENTS.md section if one exists; create one if not.
notes: Added pre-1.0 stability policy section to the crate-level rustdoc covering: SharingBackend trait (methods MAY be added with CHANGELOG/deprecation signals), handle_* functions (signatures stable within minor), register_sharing_handlers (dispatcher-mutation contract stable), URI re-exports (RFC 9670 normative), jmap_server re-exports (pin upstream major version), memory module (opt-in, may break in any minor). Resolves the gap where the previous statement applied only to the memory feature.
title: Pre-1.0 stability statement only on memory module — handler functions, SharingBackend trait, URI re-exports have no stability guidance
